Six call sites in `openmrs-module-webservices.rest` call `saveLocation`. Three are production code and three are tests. The production callers are:

1. **`LocationResource1_8.save`** (`openmrs1_8/LocationResource1_8.java:223`) returns the result of `Context.getLocationService().saveLocation(location)`. This is the main REST create/update path for locations, so it is the most directly affected.
2. **`LocationAttributeResource1_9.save`** (`openmrs1_9/LocationAttributeResource1_9.java:101`) adds the attribute to its parent location and saves the parent.
3. **`LocationAttributeResource1_9.delete`** (`openmrs1_9/LocationAttributeResource1_9.java:113`) voids the attribute and saves the parent, so a change in `saveLocation` affects attribute deletion too.

The three test call sites are in `LocationController1_9Test.java` (lines 164, 225, 242). They set up data with `service.saveLocation`, and they would break if its behaviour changed.

I did not check `openmrs-core` for other callers. The `saveLocation` definitions are in `LocationService.java:68`, `LocationServiceImpl.java:67`, `LocationDAO.java:33` and `HibernateLocationDAO.java:56`.
